daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

DPR Speaker Lodewijk Freidrich "Dasco" Parolinggoan and Deputy Speaker Saan Mustopha met demonstrating students outside the parliament building, addressing them from atop a command vehicle. Dasco chanted support for students and the Indonesian people, while the DPR pledged to bring student concerns regarding fuel prices and the MBG school meal program to the government. Dasco also placed phone calls to ministers Nanik Deyang and Bahlil in front of the demonstrators.

  • The Home Affairs Minister instructed regional governments to strengthen coordination amid widespread demonstrations across the country.
  • A DPR leader stated that 16 Trisakti University students remain suspects in a case but have not yet been processed legally.
  • The DPR claimed before demonstrators that the MBG budget would save Rp 70 trillion in government spending.
  • The Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) affirmed it will not duplicate the MBG corruption case already being handled by the Attorney General's Office.
  • West Java Governor Dedi Mulyadi threatened to revoke free school subsidies from students involved in brawls.
  • The Karawang regent asserted that the reshuffle of 151 officials was purely performance-based and free from transactional considerations.
  • Police arrested Roy Suryo in connection with the Jokowi diploma case, while also detaining Dokter Tifa whose GERD condition worsened due to high stress.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesian observer Dino Patti Djalal stated that Indonesia needs to push for compliance with the US-Iran memorandum of understanding to support peace. Migrant Watch urged the government to establish a task force to protect Indonesian migrant workers, while also calling on Malaysia to thoroughly investigate the abuse of Indonesian workers there.

Other

The Presidential Palace confirmed the MBG school meal program will continue but its governance will be evaluated, as the program faced criticism from business operators who protested the suspension during school holidays. The government expressed confidence that Indonesia will maintain its MSCI emerging market status, while also expressing optimism about retaining its classification despite market concerns.

  • The government is accelerating completion of 10 new toll road segments by December 2026.
  • Vice President Gibran inspected the 95 percent complete Bulango Ulu Dam in Gorontalo province.
  • The Home Affairs Minister and Housing Minister signed a joint decree to accelerate the 3 million homes program, while the Home Minister also inspected recipients of home renovation assistance to expand access to decent housing.
  • Indonesia will form a special task force to mitigate the impacts of El Niño weather patterns.
  • The Giant Sea Wall project will be combined with mangrove restoration efforts, according to a minister.
